subject: ventures/saas-seat-true-up
professional: a SaaS procurement / software asset management (SAM) analyst who prepares renewal negotiations; first checks: is 'avoidable' spend only what can actually be cut (reductions land at renewal, behind a notice window and any contracted minimum), is the notice deadline date right, and is overage priced the way true-up invoices bill it.

evidence.correctness: Ran /tmp/claude-0/audit-saas-seat-true-up/probe.mjs (TZ=America/New_York) against the shipped calc.mjs. Arithmetic recomputed by hand matches: 20/14/$18/4 mo -> 6 unused, 70%, $108/mo, $432 remaining, $1,296/yr; 17-seat minimum -> 3 droppable, 3 locked, $648/yr; 25 used vs 20 at 15% premium -> 5 x 18 x 1.15 = $103.50/mo, $414 term, $1,242/yr. Notice deadlines counted back on a calendar: 2026-12-31 minus 60 days = 2026-11-01, 2027-01-15 minus 60 = 2026-11-16, 2028-03-01 minus 1 = 2028-02-29 (leap), all match, DST-safe. Not 3: the headline tile labels remainingAvoidable ($432) 'avoidable through renewal' (index.html:59,156) while the page's own FAQ (index.html:74-77) says that same $432 is 'you are going to pay regardless ... usually sunk', so the second-largest number on screen means the opposite of its label; and a renewal date already in the past (2024-06-01, 30 days) yields 'the next window to act closes around 2025-05-02', a date 18 months ago (calc.mjs:125).
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature works end to end in the module tests and code: calculation, overage premium, seat minimum, notice deadline verdict, save/restore (localStorage), reset, share link carrying renewalDate/noticeDays, opt-out usage counter honoring DNT/GPC, four SEO/comparison pages, llms.txt, sitemap. node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder origins. No stubs or TODOs. Live page unreachable from this container (curl 000).
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 67 tests, 67 pass, 0.64 s. quality_mutate.py: 5 seeded mutants, 4 caught (Math.max->Math.min in droppable seats, overage premium /100->/1000, annualOverage *12 -> *months, next-window 365->366 days); the 14-day 'deadline soon' boundary (<= 14 -> < 14) survived. No test renders index.html's tile labels, so the 'avoidable through renewal' mislabel and its contradiction with the FAQ are invisible to the suite.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (145 lines), share.mjs, usage.mjs, the index.html module script, calc.test.mjs. Small pure modules, field list single-sourced in INPUT_FIELDS, every storage access wrapped, errors clear stale figures. Defects: Number('') = 0 so a blank field computes as 0 (browser `required` blocks submit, but Save scenario and a hand-edited link still accept it); formatMoney has no thousands separator ('$1296.00' on a finance page); fractional seats (20.5) accepted silently; noticeMessage ignores daysUntilRenewal so a past renewal is described as upcoming.
evidence.claims: Checked: worked example $108/$432/$1,296 (pass, recomputed); 17-seat minimum example 6 unused / 3 droppable (pass); 'no network requests' (index.html imports only local modules, pass); disclaimer present in footer and README (pass); share link carries notice fields (share.mjs, pass). Fail: the '$432 avoidable through renewal' tile and the SEO page's '$432 in avoidable spend' (how-many-unused-saas-seats-am-i-paying-for.html:43,49) contradict the FAQ's 'sunk'; README:17 lists three usage events but the page also records share_link_copied and scenario_from_link; vs-zylo.html:64 says 'this page remembers nothing between renewals' though Save scenario persists it.
evidence.fitness: Walked a renewal prep: a SAM analyst can size one subscription's unused seats, see a minimum floor and a missed-notice warning in under a minute, and share the scenario by link. Gaps hit in the first hour: one tool at a time (FAQ says add the annual figures up by hand), monthly per-seat price only although most B2B SaaS is priced and billed annually, no tiered/volume pricing, no prorated overage, and the remaining-term figure presented as avoidable. Useful as a quick sizer, not as the number to put in front of a vendor.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard true-up practice (e.g. Microsoft/Atlassian/Salesforce-style annual true-ups and typical MSA renewal clauses): reductions take effect only at renewal (the page says so in its FAQ and notice logic), but the remaining-term 'avoidable' figure treats unused seats as recoverable mid-term; overage on a true-up invoice is usually prorated from the date the seat was added to the anniversary, whereas the tool multiplies a full month by months remaining (an upper bound, not stated as such); next-window estimate assumes an annual term (stated). Seat minimum and notice-window handling are sound.

mutations.change: deadlineSoon: daysUntilDeadline >= 0 && daysUntilDeadline <= 14 -> deadlineSoon: daysUntilDeadline >= 0 && daysUntilDeadline < 14

defects.what: The results tile shows remainingAvoidable ($432 on the example) labelled 'avoidable through renewal', while the page's own FAQ says that remaining-term figure is 'you are going to pay regardless ... usually sunk'; reductions normally land only at renewal, so the label tells a buyer to claim a saving they cannot get. The SEO page repeats it ('$432 in avoidable spend').

noticeMessage never checks daysUntilRenewal: a renewal date in the past is described as 'This renewal auto-renews' and the 'next window' is deadline + 365 days, which can itself be in the past (2024-06-01 renewal -> 'next window closes around 2025-05-02' on 2026-11-20).

Overage through the remaining term is a full monthly overage times months remaining; true-up invoices usually prorate from the date each seat was added, and most B2B SaaS is priced annually, not per month. Not stated as an upper bound.
The 14-day 'deadline soon' boundary is untested: changing <= 14 to < 14 leaves all 67 tests green; no test renders the tile labels.
README lists three local usage events; the page also records share_link_copied and scenario_from_link.
Comparison page says 'this page remembers nothing between renewals' although Save scenario persists totals in the browser.

calculateTrueUp coerces a blank string to 0 (Number('')), so a blank purchased field computes as 14 seats over and $3,024/yr overage; only the form's `required` attribute guards the submit path, not Save or a hand-edited link. formatMoney also prints no thousands separator ('$1296.00').

verdict: A small, clean, browser-local seat true-up sizer whose arithmetic is right: hand recomputation of the worked example, the 17-seat-minimum case, a 15%-premium overage and three calendar-counted notice deadlines (including DST and a leap day) all match, and 67 tests pass with 4 of 5 seeded mutants caught. It misses the bar on correctness and claims: its second headline tile labels the remaining-term cost 'avoidable through renewal' while its own FAQ calls the same $432 sunk, a past renewal date produces a 'next window' that is also in the past, and the README and the Zylo comparison drift from what the page does. A procurement analyst could use it to size one subscription quickly, but not to carry the headline numbers into a vendor negotiation unchecked; it handles one tool at a time, monthly pricing only, and unprorated overage.
